# Feature: Drshya Foundations

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-061
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_ui.md` (§2 row FEAT-061; §3 Tech Stack Additions; D8; §6 "Surfaces and flow"; §7 untrusted text, CSP and no third-party requests; §8 "Dependency direction", "Delivery milestones" M1/M4, "Sequencing" item 1; §9; §10 Accessibility I9; §12 FEAT-061; §14 WCAG line; §15 visual-regression baselines; §17 I9). Values come from `.spec-lite/ui_brainstorm.md` §"Design Language: Drshya".

Every screen of the Yantra app is built from **Drshya**, Yantra's own design system, published as `@yantra/ui` in `packages/ui`. FEAT-061 lays the foundation that every later app feature styles itself with. Nothing in it is user-visible on its own until FEAT-065 ships the app shell. Its value is that later features cannot drift from the design language, from accessibility, or from the security rules. The machinery enforces this, not review.

1. **Tokens are one source of truth.** Colors are defined in OKLCH in three tiers: primitive, semantic and component. Tailwind v4 `@theme` turns the semantic tier into utilities (`bg-surface`, `text-ink-2`). Light and dark themes follow the OS or an explicit `data-theme`. Every declared text pairing must pass WCAG contrast, or the token build fails.
2. **Glass is legible by construction.** Glass is translucent, with blur. Its minimum tint opacity (the _scrim floor_) is **computed** so that glass text meets 4.5:1 over any backdrop between pure black and pure white. Solid mode swaps every glass surface for an opaque one. It turns on through `data-surfaces="solid"`, or automatically when the OS asks for reduced transparency.
3. **Type, space, radius and motion are tokens.** Archivo and Martian Mono are self-hosted, so the app makes no third-party requests. Each of the three voices (human, agent, engine) gets one utility. Reduced motion stops every loop.
4. **One icon registry.** Components never import Lucide directly. They use semantic names (`outcome.fulfilled`, `action.stop`), and six custom glyphs are drawn on Lucide's grid.
5. **Accessible primitives on React Aria Components, grown per milestone.**
   - **M1** (for the Ledger and run results): Button, Link, Table (virtualized, cursor-paged), Tabs, Tooltip, Disclosure and Toast.
   - **M4**: TextField, NumberField, Checkbox, Switch, Select, ComboBox, Dialog, Popover and Menu.
6. **Lint enforces the design system.** A raw palette utility, a hex or `oklch()` literal, an arbitrary color value, a non-custom-property inline style, or a direct `lucide-react` import fails lint. So does a Node built-in, `@yantra/core` or `@yantra/agent` import inside `packages/ui`.
7. **A gallery and harnesses prove it.** Every primitive renders in a gallery in four states (light and dark, Glass and Solid). A real-Chrome harness then checks it:
   - screenshots each state against a visual baseline;
   - runs `axe-core` on each state;
   - checks that focus is visible;
   - serves the gallery under the app's own `Content-Security-Policy` and fails on any CSP violation or any request to another origin.

**Acceptance (plan §12 FEAT-061).**

- Every primitive renders in the gallery in light and dark, Glass and Solid, with visual baselines.
- Every text pairing passes contrast, including Ion on both themes. Glass text passes analytically against black and white.
- `axe-core` reports no violations in the gallery.
- Lint fails on a raw palette utility or a direct `lucide-react` import.
- The package imports nothing from core, agent or Node built-ins.
- Focus is visible everywhere.

**Milestone split.** TASK-001 to TASK-011 are the **M1 subset** that FEAT-065 and FEAT-066 need (plan §8 Sequencing item 1). TASK-012 to TASK-014 are the **M4 "remaining primitive catalogue"**. They can land later without reopening any M1 task.

### Pre-check findings (computed while writing this spec)

The brainstorm's OKLCH values were run through the WCAG 2.x contrast formula. The OKLCH-to-sRGB conversion was clipped to gamut, and glass was modeled as source-over compositing in gamma-encoded sRGB. TASK-002 and TASK-004 re-derive every number below in code. The numbers here say only what those tasks will find.

| Pairing                                                         | Ratio                             | Required           | Result                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Light: white on the Ion fill `0.55 0.14 218`                    | 4.39                              | 4.5                | **fails**                                            |
| Light: Jade `0.55 0.13 162` as text on fog-00 / fog-05 / fog-10 | 4.42 / 4.18 / 3.91                | 4.5                | **fails**                                            |
| Light: Amber `0.62 0.15 65` as text on fog-00 / fog-05 / fog-10 | 3.71 / 3.51 / 3.28                | 4.5                | **fails** (passes 3:1 as a graphic)                  |
| Light: Crimson, Rani, Ion ink, ink, ink-2, ink-3 on fog-00…10   | ≥ 4.59                            | 4.5                | pass                                                 |
| Dark: every signal, Ion ink, ink, ink-2, ink-3 on fog-90…99     | ≥ 5.15                            | 4.5                | pass                                                 |
| Dark: on-accent on the Ion fill `0.80 0.14 218`                 | 10.44                             | 4.5                | pass                                                 |
| Glass floor for `ink`: light / dark (no noise; with 0.03 noise) | α ≥ 0.485 / 0.590 (0.500 / 0.610) | recipe 0.66 / 0.72 | recipe suffices                                      |
| Glass floor for `ink-2`: light / dark                           | α ≥ 0.750 / 0.775 (0.775 / 0.800) | recipe 0.66 / 0.72 | **floor raises the tint**                            |
| Glass floor for `accent-ink`: light / dark                      | α ≥ 0.920 / 0.715 (0.945 / 0.735) | —                  | not allowed as glass text (light fails the 0.85 cap) |
| Glass floor for `ink-3`: light / dark                           | α ≥ 0.940 / 0.905 (0.970 / 0.930) | —                  | not allowed as glass text                            |
| Field boundary: fog-30 on fog-00 (light)                        | 1.49                              | 3.0 (non-text)     | **fails**; fog-60 gives 5.19                         |

### Deviations (awaiting confirmation)

- **DEVIATION D1 (Ion light fill).** The brainstorm requires the light Ion fill with white text to pass 4.5:1 in CI, but its own value gives 4.39:1. **Proposal:** lower the light fill's lightness from 0.55 to 0.54 (`0.54 0.14 218`), the largest value in 0.005 steps that passes, and keep hue and chroma. The dark fill is unchanged. **Confirmed by the user 2026-11-04.**
- **DEVIATION D2 (Jade and Amber as text in light theme).** Light Jade (3.91–4.42) and light Amber (3.28–3.71) fail 4.5:1 as text on the light surfaces. **Proposal:** split each signal into two tokens, the same approach that gives Ion two fills:
  - `signal-<name>` is the **graphic** token, for glyphs, fills and rings, and must reach 3:1 non-text contrast. It keeps the brainstorm value.
  - `signal-<name>-ink` is the **text** token and must reach 4.5:1. In the light theme it lowers lightness to the largest passing value against fog-10, the worst case: Jade ink `0.51 0.13 162`, Amber ink `0.54 0.15 65`. Crimson and Rani ink equal their graphic values in light, and every dark ink equals its graphic value.

  **Confirmed by the user 2026-11-04.**

- **DEVIATION D3 (where the gallery lives).** The plan calls the gallery an in-app `/gallery` route, but `apps/web` is created by FEAT-065, and FEAT-061 must be able to start first (§8 Sequencing item 1). **Proposal:**
  - The gallery is a React component exported from `@yantra/ui/gallery`.
  - A small standalone Vite page inside `packages/ui` serves it for development and for the harness, built into `packages/ui/dist/gallery/`.
  - FEAT-065 mounts the same component at `/gallery` in development builds of `apps/web`.

  The route still exists in development builds only, as §6 requires, and no Storybook is added. **Confirmed by the user 2026-11-04.**

- **DEVIATION D4 (light signals are out of the sRGB gamut; found at implementation).** The pre-check clipped OKLCH to gamut, but §2 makes an out-of-gamut token a generator error. Six light tokens are outside sRGB at their brainstorm chroma (Ion fill's red channel is −0.06). On a wide-gamut display Chrome would render the unclipped color, which the gate never measured. **Decision (user, 2026-11-04):** keep the gamut error, and store each of these tokens at its lightness and hue with the largest in-gamut chroma, floored to 0.001. Lightness and hue are unchanged, so D1 and D2 stand. Every pairing still passes:

  | Token (light)          | Brainstorm chroma | In-gamut chroma | Check          | Clipped | Shipped |
  | ---------------------- | ----------------- | --------------- | -------------- | ------- | ------- |
  | `ion-fill` (0.54, 218) | 0.14              | 0.097           | white on fill  | 4.56    | 4.89    |
  | `accent-ink` (0.50)    | 0.12              | 0.089           | text on fog-10 | 4.80    | 5.06    |
  | `jade` (0.55, 162)     | 0.13              | 0.120           | 3:1 on fog-10  | 3.91    | 3.97    |
  | `jade-ink` (0.51)      | 0.13              | 0.111           | text on fog-10 | 4.58    | 4.72    |
  | `amber` (0.62, 65)     | 0.15              | 0.139           | 3:1 on fog-10  | 3.28    | 3.28    |
  | `amber-ink` (0.54)     | 0.15              | 0.121           | text on fog-10 | 4.55    | 4.55    |

  The dark theme, Crimson and Rani are already in gamut. When a token is out of gamut, the generator still measures its contrast on the clipped color, so one `TokenContractError` lists the gamut failure and any contrast failure together.

### Spec decisions

The plan leaves these details open. Each is the smallest rule that makes the plan's behavior enforceable. Override any of them before Implement starts.

| #   | Decision                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| S1  | **Primitive ramps never become utilities.** They are emitted as plain custom properties on `:root` (`--drshya-fog-00`, `--drshya-ion-fill`, …). Only the semantic tier is declared in `@theme` (`--color-bg`, `--color-ink-2`, …), and component knobs are plain properties (`--button-*`, `--ring-*`, `--hud-*`). The generated `@theme` also clears Tailwind's default namespaces that Drshya replaces (`--color-*`, `--radius-*`, `--shadow-*`, `--inset-shadow-*`, `--drop-shadow-*`, `--font-*`, `--text-*`, `--animate-*`). As a result, `bg-red-500`, `bg-fog-10` and `rounded-2xl` produce no CSS at all, and lint (TASK-006) is a second wall, not the only one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | The brainstorm says primitives are "never used by components". If a utility does not exist, it cannot be used by accident. Clearing `--radius-*` also enforces the banned "`rounded-2xl` everywhere" pattern. |
| S2  | **TypeScript token data is the single source; the CSS is generated.** `src/tokens/*.ts` holds every value. `scripts/emit-tokens.ts` writes `src/styles/theme.generated.css`. A drift test re-emits the file in memory and compares it byte for byte (normalizing CRLF), and the generated file is listed in `.prettierignore`. This is the same pattern as `packages/protocol/generated`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | The contrast gate and the scrim floor must compute from exactly the values the CSS ships. Hand-writing the same values in two places is a silent divergence (memory → Coding Standards).                      |
| S3  | **The glass model.** The composite is source-over in gamma-encoded sRGB, which is how Chrome composites. The backdrop is any color in the sRGB cube: relative luminance is monotonic in each channel, so black and white are the two extremes, and blur and `saturate()` keep colors inside the cube.<br>• The **floor** is the smallest α, in 0.005 steps rounded up, at which every token in the theme's `GLASS_TEXT_TOKENS` reaches 4.5:1 over both black and white. The worst-case noise layer is applied too: the composite is shifted toward black and toward white by `--glass-noise-alpha`.<br>• The tint opacity used is `max(recipe, floor)`, where the recipe is 0.66 light and 0.72 dark.<br>• `GLASS_TEXT_TOKENS` is `ink` and `ink-2` in both themes. A token may join the set only if its computed floor, with noise, stays at or below 0.85 in **both** themes; the generator enforces this cap. `ink-3` and `accent-ink` are never glass text. On glass, Ion appears only as a graphic (the focus ring, icons and fills), never as text. | "Sampling is regression evidence only" (§12). The pre-check shows that `ink-3`, and light `accent-ink`, would need an almost opaque tint, which would no longer be glass.                                     |
| S4  | Signals have a graphic token and a text token (DEVIATION D2). `Aborted` has no signal token: it uses `ink-2` with the ban glyph, as the brainstorm says.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Status is never shown by color alone (banned patterns), and text must reach 4.5:1.                                                                                                                            |
| S5  | **The gallery is a component plus a dev page** (DEVIATION D3). The page's state comes from the query string: `?entry=<id>&theme=light\|dark\|system&surfaces=glass\|solid`. A gallery completeness test fails if any export of `src/primitives/index.ts` has no gallery entry.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | The completeness test is what keeps the "every primitive renders in the gallery" acceptance true as the catalogue grows.                                                                                      |
| S6  | **Visual baselines are per platform; only Linux is required.** Baselines live in `e2e/drshya/baselines/<process.platform>/<entry>--<theme>--<surfaces>.png`.<br>• **Linux** (CI `ubuntu-latest`): a missing or mismatched baseline fails.<br>• **Windows and macOS:** the harness compares when a baseline exists, and otherwise skips the pixel step with an explicit `ctx.skip` reason. axe, CSP, origin and focus checks still run on every OS.<br>• `UPDATE_DRSHYA_BASELINES=1` writes baselines.<br>• On failure, CI uploads `e2e/drshya/.out/` (actual and diff PNGs), so a Linux baseline can be committed from a Windows machine.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | This resolves plan §15 "per-OS or Linux-only in CI" without tripling maintenance: font rasterization differs per OS. **Confirmed by the user 2026-11-04.**                                                    |
| S7  | **Appearance is a data contract, not a store.** `Appearance = {theme: 'system'\|'light'\|'dark', surfaces: 'glass'\|'solid'}` maps to `data-theme` and `data-surfaces` on the root element. `theme: 'system'` removes `data-theme`. FEAT-061 provides the mapping and `applyAppearance`. FEAT-065 reads the `ui.theme` and `ui.surfaces` preferences and calls it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | The preferences are FEAT-065 scope (§12 FEAT-065 "Preferences"). The gallery needs the same contract now.                                                                                                     |
| S8  | **The toast queue belongs to the app.** `createToastQueue()` returns an instance, which `<ToastProvider queue>` supplies. There is no module-level queue.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | No hidden singletons (memory → Architecture; plan §9).                                                                                                                                                        |
| S9  | **`Link` treats every URL as untrusted.**<br>• An absolute `http:`/`https:` URL opens in a new browsing context, always with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, and shows the `action.openExternal` icon plus visually hidden "(opens in a new tab)".<br>• An app-relative path stays in the app.<br>• Any other scheme (`javascript:`, `data:`, `file:`, `blob:`, unparsable) renders as inert text, never as a link.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Plan §7: page-derived URLs are untrusted, and external links carry `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. A primitive that cannot emit a `javascript:` link removes the bug class for every later surface.              |
| S10 | **Dependency gate.** TASK-001 presents §3's packages to the user, with the exact current stable versions read from the registry at that time, and pins them **exactly** (no `^`) only after approval. Two additions go beyond §3 and need explicit approval:<br>• `@testing-library/dom`, the required peer of `@testing-library/react`;<br>• `@testing-library/user-event`, because React Aria's press and keyboard handling is driven by pointer and keyboard event sequences that `fireEvent` does not produce. If it is declined, the tests use `fireEvent` with React Aria's documented pointer-event sequence.<br>The e2e workspace reuses the root's `puppeteer-core` version (`25.10.0`, the same as core). The gallery's `vite` is the current stable major at or above 6.4.4 (TODO: the Vitest 4 migration lists the vite 5 advisory).                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Memory → Dependencies: check with the user before pinning a new dependency. Plan §3: specs pin exact versions.                                                                                                |
| S11 | **No Compact density.** The spacing base stays Tailwind's `--spacing` (0.25rem, the brainstorm's 4 px base), so Phase 2 can scale one variable.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `ui.density` is not added until Phase 2 (§6, §13).                                                                                                                                                            |
| S12 | **CSP-safe assets.** The gallery's Vite build sets `build.assetsInlineLimit: 0`, so fonts and the glass noise texture are emitted as files, never `data:` URIs, which `default-src 'self'` would block. The harness serves the gallery under exactly §7's policy. FEAT-065 must keep the same Vite setting for `apps/web`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | §7: strict `default-src 'self'`, and no third-party requests.                                                                                                                                                 |

**Implementation notes (recorded during Implement).**

- **Gallery output directories.** `tsc` emits `src/gallery/` to `dist/gallery/`, so `@yantra/ui/gallery` resolves to `dist/gallery/index.{js,d.ts}`, and the standalone page builds to `dist/gallery-site/` (not `dist/gallery-module` and `dist/gallery` as §3 and TASK-003 said). The harness serves `dist/gallery-site`.
- **axe injection.** `page.addScriptTag({ path })` adds an inline `<script>`, which `default-src 'self'` blocks. The harness evaluates axe's source with `page.evaluate` (`Runtime.evaluate`), which CSP does not govern, after it has collected the CSP evidence.
- **Theme selectors.** The explicit theme blocks are `[data-theme="dark"]` and `[data-theme="light"]` rather than `:root[...]`, so any subtree can carry the appearance. The gallery wrapper needs this. The OS block stays `:root:not([data-theme="light"])`.
- **Linux baselines are bootstrapped by CI.** The baselines could not be produced on the implementing Windows machine. The first Linux CI run fails the pixel step and uploads `e2e/drshya/.out/`, and those images are committed as `e2e/drshya/baselines/linux/` (S6 flow).
- **Glass numbers after D4.** The shipped `--glass-alpha` is 0.775 (light) and 0.8 (dark), set by `ink-2`, as the pre-check predicted. D4 lowered `accent-ink`'s chroma, which moves its light glass floor from 0.945 to 0.925. That is still above the 0.85 cap, so it stays off glass, and TASK-004's test asserts 0.925.
- **Glass verification without disabling noise.** The noise tile is exactly half black and half white with a 64 px period, so any 64×64 window averages to `base + noise·(0.5 − base)`. The harness checks that mean against the S3 model to ±3/255 over black and white in both themes. `prefers-reduced-transparency` is emulated through CDP `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia`, because puppeteer's `emulateMediaFeatures` rejects that feature.
- **Gallery fixtures stylesheet.** The black, white and stripe backdrops live in `src/gallery/gallery.css`, exported as `@yantra/ui/gallery.css`. FEAT-065 imports it next to `drshya.css` wherever it mounts the gallery.
- **Glyphs are path data.** Each `src/icons/glyphs/*.ts` file exports only its geometry (`GlyphNode`). `registry.tsx`, the only file allowed to import `lucide-react`, wraps each one with Lucide's own `createLucideIcon`, so glyphs get Lucide's exact SVG contract by construction. Lucide's half-filled circle is named `Contrast` in 1.68.0, and it backs `outcome.partial`.
- **React Aria under the strict CSP.** React Aria's `usePress` injects `<style id="react-aria-pressable-style">`, which `default-src 'self'` blocks; the harness caught it on the first primitive. Drshya ships that `touch-action` rule in `drshya.css` (`@layer base`). `prepareStrictCsp(document)` from `@yantra/ui` places a `<meta>` with that id, so React Aria skips the injection. **FEAT-065 must call `prepareStrictCsp` before its first render.** `usePreventScroll` has a second injection, but only on iOS Safari's scroll path. A unit test pins the id against the installed React Aria source.
- **Focus ring.** The focus ring is `outline-hidden focus-visible:outline-solid focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-accent`. Tailwind v4's `outline-none` also sets `--tw-outline-style: none`, which would leave the ring invisible. Buttons transition only `color`, `background-color` and `border-color`, so the ring appears at once. The harness focus walk measures two animation frames after each Tab.
- **Pairing added.** `on-accent` on `accent-ink` is in the gate, because `accent-ink` is the primary button's hover and pressed fill.
- **Primitive families.** A primitive can span several exports (`Tabs`, `TabList`, `Tab`, `TabPanel`), so `src/primitives/families.ts` maps each family to its exports. `GalleryEntry.primitive` names the family. The completeness test checks both directions: every barrel export belongs to exactly one family, and every family has exactly one gallery entry. This is what makes TASK-014's "all 16 primitives" countable.
- **Pinned React Aria API status (1.22.1).** Toast is still exported as `UNSTABLE_ToastRegion`, `UNSTABLE_ToastQueue` and `UNSTABLE_Toast`. `TableLoadMoreItem` and `SubmenuTrigger` exist. jsdom needs a `CSS.escape` polyfill (`tests/support/css-escape.ts`) for React Aria collections.
- **Lint-staged.** The ESLint command in `lint-staged` gained `--no-warn-ignored`. Without it, committing a new `_lint-fixtures` file fails `--max-warnings=0` with "File ignored" warnings.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does not exist, and FEAT-061 persists nothing. Its "data model" is the typed contracts that the token generator, the gallery and later features share. All of them live in `packages/ui/src` and are plain TypeScript types: this package has no Zod and no protocol schema. Nothing is written to `~/.yantra`.

### Entities & Attributes

- **`Oklch`** (`src/tokens/color-math.ts`):
  - `l` (number) — lightness, 0..1.
  - `c` (number) — chroma, ≥ 0.
  - `h` (number) — hue in degrees, 0..360.
  - Rendered as `oklch(L C H)`. Conversion to sRGB clips to gamut and reports `inGamut: boolean` (a token out of gamut is a generator error).
- **`PrimitiveToken`** (`src/tokens/palette.ts`):
  - `name` (string literal) — e.g. `fog-05`, `ion-fill`, `jade`, `jade-ink`.
  - `light` (`Oklch`) — value in the light theme.
  - `dark` (`Oklch`) — value in the dark theme. Fog steps are theme-independent, so both values are equal.
  - Emitted as `--drshya-<name>`, never as a utility.
- **`SemanticColor`** (closed union, `src/tokens/semantic.ts`):
  - **Values:** `bg`, `surface`, `sunken`, `ink`, `ink-2`, `ink-3`, `rule`, `rule-strong`, `field-edge`, `accent`, `on-accent`, `accent-ink`, `signal-{fulfilled,partial,failed,needs-you}`, `signal-{fulfilled,partial,failed,needs-you}-ink`, `glass-tint`, `glass-edge`, `glass-spec`.
  - **Mapping:** `SEMANTIC_COLORS: Record<SemanticColor, { light: PrimitiveName; dark: PrimitiveName }>`.
  - **Initial mapping.** The brainstorm leaves the dark `ink`, dark `rule` and dark `sunken` roles open; this spec fills them.

    | Semantic                    | Light                                       | Dark                     |
    | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
    | `bg`                        | fog-05                                      | fog-99                   |
    | `surface`                   | fog-00                                      | fog-95                   |
    | `sunken`                    | fog-10                                      | fog-99                   |
    | `ink`                       | fog-95                                      | fog-05                   |
    | `ink-2`                     | fog-70                                      | fog-40                   |
    | `ink-3`                     | fog-60                                      | fog-50                   |
    | `rule`                      | fog-20                                      | fog-90                   |
    | `rule-strong`               | fog-30                                      | fog-80                   |
    | `field-edge`                | fog-60                                      | fog-50                   |
    | `accent`                    | ion-fill `0.54 0.097 218` (D1, D4)          | ion-fill `0.80 0.14 218` |
    | `on-accent`                 | white `1 0 0`                               | `0.18 0.03 230`          |
    | `accent-ink`                | `0.50 0.089 218` (D4)                       | `0.82 0.12 218`          |
    | `signal-fulfilled` / `-ink` | `0.55 0.12 162` / `0.51 0.111 162` (D2, D4) | `0.76 0.14 162` / same   |
    | `signal-partial` / `-ink`   | `0.62 0.139 65` / `0.54 0.121 65` (D2, D4)  | `0.80 0.14 65` / same    |
    | `signal-failed` / `-ink`    | `0.55 0.20 25` / same                       | `0.70 0.18 25` / same    |
    | `signal-needs-you` / `-ink` | `0.55 0.22 352` / same                      | `0.72 0.20 352` / same   |
    | `glass-tint`                | fog-00                                      | fog-95                   |
    | `glass-edge`, `glass-spec`  | fog-20, fog-00                              | fog-80, fog-40           |

- **`ContrastPairing`** (`src/tokens/pairings.ts`):
  - `fg` (`SemanticColor`) — the text or graphic color.
  - `bg` (`SemanticColor | 'glass'`) — the color it sits on. `'glass'` means "the glass composite over black and over white".
  - `kind` (`'text' | 'non-text'`) — sets the minimum: 4.5 for `text`, 3.0 for `non-text`.
  - `themes` (`readonly ('light' | 'dark')[]`) — the themes in which the pairing applies.
  - **Initial set:**
    - every ink (`ink`, `ink-2`, `ink-3`, `accent-ink`, `signal-*-ink`) on `bg`, `surface` and `sunken`;
    - `on-accent` on `accent`;
    - `surface` on `ink` (tooltips);
    - `signal-*` (graphic) and `field-edge` as `non-text` on `bg`, `surface` and `sunken`;
    - `accent` as `non-text` on `bg` and `surface` (the focus ring);
    - `GLASS_TEXT_TOKENS` on `'glass'`.
- **`GlassSpec`** (`src/tokens/glass.ts`):
  - `recipeAlpha` (`{light: 0.66, dark: 0.72}`) — the brainstorm's tint opacity.
  - `noiseAlpha` (number, initial `0.03`) — the maximum opacity of the noise texture.
  - `blurPx` (`20`) — the backdrop blur.
  - `saturate` (`1.5`) — the backdrop saturation.
  - `floorAlpha` (`{light: number; dark: number}`) — **computed** by the generator, never hand-set.
  - `tintAlpha` (`{light: number; dark: number}`) — `max(recipeAlpha, floorAlpha)`, emitted as `--glass-alpha`.
- **`TypeScale`, `RadiusScale`, `MotionScale`** (`src/tokens/scale.ts`):
  - **Type:** `micro 0.72rem`, `caption 0.8125rem`, `body 0.9375rem`, `lead 1.125rem`, `title 1.5rem`, `headline 2.25rem`, `display clamp(2.25rem, 1rem + 4vw, 4.1rem)`, each with a line height.
  - **Radius:** `chip 4px`, `control 8px`, `frame 14px`, `full 9999px`.
  - **Motion:** `quick 120ms`, `base 200ms`, `slow 320ms`, and `standard` easing `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`.
  - **Font families:** `sans`, `mono`.
- **`IconName`** (closed union, `src/icons/registry.tsx`) — dotted semantic names. The registry maps each name to one of:
  - `{ source: 'lucide'; component: LucideIcon }`;
  - `{ source: 'glyph'; component: GlyphComponent }`.
- **`Appearance`** (`src/appearance.ts`):
  - `theme` (`'system' | 'light' | 'dark'`) — `system` removes `data-theme`.
  - `surfaces` (`'glass' | 'solid'`) — sets `data-surfaces`.
- **`GalleryEntry`** (`src/gallery/entries.tsx`):
  - `id` (kebab-case string, unique) — used in the URL and in baseline file names.
  - `title` (string).
  - `primitive` (string | null) — the export name from `src/primitives/index.ts`, or `null` for token or icon sheets.
  - `render` (`() => ReactNode`) — renders the entry deterministically: fixed data and no clocks.
  - `interactive` (boolean) — whether the harness runs the focus-visible walk on it.

### Relationships

- `SemanticColor` N:1 `PrimitiveToken` per theme via `SEMANTIC_COLORS`.
- `ContrastPairing` references two `SemanticColor`s, or one plus the glass composite.
- `GlassSpec.floorAlpha` is derived from `GLASS_TEXT_TOKENS` × {black, white} × {±noise}.
- `GalleryEntry.primitive` 1:1 with each export of `src/primitives/index.ts` (completeness test).
- `IconName` 1:1 with a registry record. Each record points to exactly one Lucide component or one custom glyph.

### Indexes & Constraints

- `SemanticColor` and `IconName` are closed unions, so adding a token or an icon is a typed change.
- Every `PrimitiveToken` must be inside the sRGB gamut in both themes, or the generator throws `TokenContractError`.
- Every `ContrastPairing` must meet its minimum in each listed theme, or the generator throws `TokenContractError` listing every failure.
- `GalleryEntry.id` values are unique, and baseline file names derive from them.
- `src/styles/theme.generated.css` is byte-identical to a fresh emit (drift test).

## 3. Files

**New package `packages/ui` (`@yantra/ui`)**

- `packages/ui/package.json` — the package manifest:
  - **exports:** `.` → `dist/index.{js,d.ts}`; `./drshya.css` → `src/styles/drshya.css`; `./gallery` → `dist/gallery-module/index.{js,d.ts}`.
  - **scripts:** `build` (`tsx scripts/emit-tokens.ts --check && tsc -b tsconfig.build.json && vite build --config gallery/vite.config.ts`), `test`, `lint`, `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`), `emit:tokens`, `clean`.
- `packages/ui/tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.build.json` — the source project:
  - `lib` is `ES2022`, `DOM` and `DOM.Iterable`; `jsx` is `react-jsx`.
  - `types: []` (no Node types in `src`).
  - It includes `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}` and excludes `src/_lint-fixtures/**`.
- `packages/ui/tsconfig.tests.json` — typechecks `tests/**` and `gallery/**` (with `vite/client` types), so test-level guarantees are real (memory → Testing).
- `packages/ui/vitest.config.ts` — sets `environment: 'jsdom'`, includes `tests/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx}`, runs `setupFiles: ['./tests/setup.ts']` and sets `css: false`.
- `packages/ui/scripts/emit-tokens.ts` — the generator CLI. It writes `src/styles/theme.generated.css`; `--check` only validates the tokens and fails on drift.
- `packages/ui/src/index.ts` — the public barrel: tokens metadata, `cn`/`tv`, `Icon`, primitives and `applyAppearance`.
- `packages/ui/src/tokens/color-math.ts` — OKLCH↔sRGB, relative luminance, contrast ratio, source-over compositing and `minimumScrimAlpha`.
- `packages/ui/src/tokens/palette.ts`, `semantic.ts`, `pairings.ts`, `glass.ts`, `scale.ts` — the token data (§2).
- `packages/ui/src/tokens/emit.ts` — the pure `emitThemeCss(): string` used by the script and the drift test.
- `packages/ui/src/tokens/errors.ts` — `TokenContractError` (a custom `Error` subclass carrying `failures: readonly TokenFailure[]`).
- `packages/ui/src/styles/drshya.css` — the hand-written entry stylesheet. It contains:
  - `@import "tailwindcss"` and the generated theme;
  - the font imports and `@plugin "tailwindcss-react-aria-components"`;
  - `@custom-variant`s for theme and surfaces;
  - the `@utility` definitions: `glass`, `type-label`, `type-display`, `type-agent`, `type-engine` and `focus-ring`;
  - the reduced-motion rules;
  - `@source "../"`.
- `packages/ui/src/styles/theme.generated.css` — **generated**; listed in `.prettierignore`.
- `packages/ui/src/styles/assets/glass-noise.png` — the noise tile, a file asset (S12).
- `packages/ui/src/appearance.ts` — the `Appearance` type, `appearanceAttributes()` and `applyAppearance(root, appearance)`.
- `packages/ui/src/lib/cn.ts` — `cn()` over `extendTailwindMerge`, configured with Drshya's color, text, radius and shadow names, plus `tv = createTV({ twMergeConfig })`.
- `packages/ui/src/icons/registry.tsx` — **the only file that may import `lucide-react`**.
- `packages/ui/src/icons/Icon.tsx` — the `Icon` component.
- `packages/ui/src/icons/glyphs/{bindu,contract,capture,handoff,protected,provenance}.tsx` — the six custom glyphs.
- `packages/ui/src/primitives/{Button,Link,Tabs,Tooltip,Disclosure,Toast,Table}.tsx` — the M1 primitives.
- `packages/ui/src/primitives/{TextField,NumberField,Checkbox,Switch,Popover,Select,ComboBox,Dialog,Menu}.tsx` — the M4 primitives.
- `packages/ui/src/primitives/field.tsx` — the shared Label, Description and FieldError anatomy (M4).
- `packages/ui/src/primitives/index.ts` — the primitives barrel that the completeness test reads.
- `packages/ui/src/gallery/{Gallery.tsx,entries.tsx,fixtures.ts,index.ts}` — the gallery component, its entries, and deterministic fixture data such as the 10,000-row table data.
- `packages/ui/gallery/{index.html,main.tsx,vite.config.ts}` — the standalone dev and harness page (S5, S12), which builds to `dist/gallery/`.
- `packages/ui/src/_lint-fixtures/*.{ts,tsx}` — files that intentionally violate the rules, for the boundary spec.
- `packages/ui/tests/**` — mirrored unit tests (listed per task).

**Repository wiring (modified)**

- `eslint.config.js` — the new `packages/ui` and `apps/web` blocks:
  - import boundary, raw color, inline style, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` and the Lucide import rule;
  - the `.spec.tsx` Vitest block;
  - the site-token rule widened to `.tsx`;
  - `packages/ui/tests/**` and `packages/ui/gallery/**` in the type-check-disabled list.
- `tsconfig.json` (references `packages/ui`), `vitest.workspace.ts` (adds `packages/ui`) and `.prettierignore` (the generated CSS).
- `package.json` (root) — `lint-staged` covers `*.{ts,tsx}` and `*.css`.
- `.gitignore` — `e2e/drshya/.out/`.
- `README.md` — adds `@yantra/ui` to the package list.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — uploads `e2e/drshya/.out/` as an artifact when the e2e step fails (S6).

**Harness (`e2e`)**

- `e2e/package.json` — adds the `@yantra/ui` workspace dependency and the dev dependencies `axe-core`, `pixelmatch`, `pngjs`, `@types/pngjs` and `puppeteer-core` (25.10.0).
- `e2e/drshya/gallery-server.ts` — a `node:http` static server for `packages/ui/dist/gallery` on `127.0.0.1:0`. It sends the §7 headers: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and an allowlisted `Content-Type`.
- `e2e/drshya/visual.ts` — the PNG compare (`pixelmatch`), the baseline update mode, and diff output to `.out/`.
- `e2e/drshya/browser.ts` — Chrome discovery through `@yantra/core`'s `detectChrome`, plus a headless puppeteer-core launch with a fixed viewport (1280×800, DPR 1).
- `e2e/drshya/baselines/linux/*.png` — the committed baselines (S6).
- `e2e/drshya-gallery.spec.ts` — the `@no-llm` harness: screenshot, `axe-core`, CSP and origin, focus-visible, fonts, glass sampling and table virtualization checks.

**Documentation (via Document update mode)**

- `docs/features/drshya-design-system.md` (new) and `docs/architecture.md`.

    - `relativeLuminance(rgb)` and `contrastRatio(a, b)` per WCAG 2.x;
    - `compositeOver(fg, alpha, backdrop)` as source-over in gamma-encoded sRGB;
    - `formatOklch(o)`.
  - **`palette.ts`:** the 13 fog steps and the light/dark signal values from §2, including D1 and D2.
  - **`semantic.ts`:** `SEMANTIC_COLORS` from §2.

  - **`src/tokens/emit.ts` → `emitThemeCss()`.** It validates first: gamut, then every pairing. It throws `TokenContractError` listing **all** failures, each with the pairing, theme, measured ratio and required ratio. It then returns the CSS:

    - `color-scheme: light` / `dark` set alongside each block, so native controls and scrollbars follow the theme.

### TASK-006: Lint refuses raw palette utilities, color literals, arbitrary color values, non-custom-property inline styles and `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in `packages/ui` and `apps/web`

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - In `eslint.config.js`, export `SITE_SPECIFIC_SELECTORS` (the two existing site-token selector objects) and a new `DRSHYA_STYLE_SELECTORS` array.
  - Add a block for `files: ['packages/ui/src/**/*.{ts,tsx}', 'apps/web/src/**/*.{ts,tsx}']` with `ignores: ['packages/ui/src/tokens/**']`. Its `no-restricted-syntax` value is `[...SITE_SPECIFIC_SELECTORS, ...DRSHYA_STYLE_SELECTORS]`. The site rule **must** be restated here: a later flat-config block replaces `no-restricted-syntax` options for matching files, so leaving it out would silently disable the site rule in `packages/ui`. `DRSHYA_STYLE_SELECTORS` catches:
    - a `Literal` or `TemplateElement` containing a **raw palette utility**: a utility prefix (`bg`, `text`, `border(-[xytrblse])?`, `ring`, `ring-offset`, `outline`, `fill`, `stroke`, `from`, `via`, `to`, `decoration`, `shadow`, `inset-shadow`, `drop-shadow`, `divide`, `placeholder`, `caret`, `accent`) followed by a Tailwind palette or Drshya primitive name (`slate`…`rose`, `black`, `white`, `fog`, `ion`, `jade`, `amber`, `crimson`, `rani`). This includes variant-prefixed forms such as `hover:bg-red-500` and opacity forms such as `/50`;
    - an **arbitrary color value**: `-[#…]`, or `-[` followed by `rgb(`, `rgba(`, `hsl(`, `hsla(`, `oklch(`, `oklab(`, `lab(`, `lch(` or `color(`;
    - a **color literal**: a literal that is exactly a hex color (`^#(?:[0-9a-f]{3,4}|[0-9a-f]{6}|[0-9a-f]{8})$`, case-insensitive, so refs like `#07` stay legal), or that contains `oklch(`, `rgb(` or `hsl(`;
    - an **inline style** with any `style={{…}}` property key that is not a string literal starting with `--` (`JSXAttribute[name.name="style"] > JSXExpressionContainer > ObjectExpression > Property` with an `Identifier` key, or a `Literal` key not matching `^--`);
    - **`JSXAttribute[name.name="dangerouslySetInnerHTML"]`** (plan §3: no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`).

    Each message cites plan §9 and memory → General (Drshya rule).

  - Keep the token data directory exempt from the style selectors only. Through the ignore, the existing site-token block still covers `src/tokens/**/*.ts`.
  - **Add fixtures** under `packages/ui/src/_lint-fixtures/`:
    - `raw-palette.tsx` (`className="bg-red-500"`, `hover:text-white`, `bg-fog-10`);
    - `arbitrary-color.tsx` (`bg-[#ff0000]`, `text-[oklch(0.5_0.1_200)]`);
    - `color-literal.tsx` (`const c = '#1a2b3c'`, `'oklch(0.5 0.1 200)'`);
    - `inline-style.tsx` (`style={{ color: 'red' }}`);
    - `inner-html.tsx`;
    - `site-name.tsx` (a site token in a literal);
    - `clean.tsx` (`bg-surface text-ink-2 border-rule`, `style={{ '--progress': '40%' }}`, a `'#07'` ref string) — must be clean.

- [ ] **Unit Tests**: extend `packages/ui/tests/boundary-rules.spec.ts`:
  - each violating fixture reports `no-restricted-syntax` with the expected message fragment, on the expected line;
  - `clean.tsx` reports nothing;
  - `site-name.tsx` still reports the site-specific message, a regression test for the flat-config replacement hazard;
  - a copy of a raw-palette literal placed under `src/tokens/` (an in-memory lint via `eslint.lintText` with that file path) reports no style violation.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for `docs/features/drshya-design-system.md` (what lint forbids and the sanctioned alternatives).

### TASK-011: Table: a virtualized, cursor-paged, accessible data table that renders 10,000 rows with a bounded DOM and asks for more only when it should

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **`Table<T>`** is built on React Aria `Table` inside React Aria `Virtualizer` with `TableLayout` (fixed `rowHeight`, default 40, and a sticky header).
  - **Props:**
    - `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (required by type);
    - `columns: readonly { id: string; header: string; cell: (row: T) => ReactNode; isRowHeader?: boolean; width?: number | string; align?: 'start' | 'end'; voice?: 'body' | 'engine' }[]` — exactly one row-header column, asserted at runtime in development;
    - `rows: readonly T[]` and `getRowKey: (row: T) => string`;
    - `onRowAction?`;
    - `loadState: 'idle' | 'loading' | 'error' | 'exhausted'` and `onLoadMore?: () => void`;
    - `emptyState: ReactNode`.
  - **Cursor paging is the caller's business.** The table renders React Aria's load-more sentinel row (verify the API name in the pinned version, e.g. `TableLoadMoreItem`). It calls `onLoadMore` when the sentinel scrolls into view, and only while `loadState === 'idle'`.
  - `loading` shows a non-looping progress row under reduced motion.
  - `error` shows a "Couldn't load more" row with a `Retry` button (`action.retry`) that calls `onLoadMore`.
  - The `engine` voice renders cells in `type-engine` (IDs, URLs, refs).
  - **Gallery entries:** `table` (25 deterministic rows, mixed voices) and `table-large` (10,000 fixture rows, `loadState: 'idle'` with a counting `onLoadMore` exposed on `window.__drshyaLoadMoreCount` for the harness).
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (`tests/primitives/table.spec.tsx`). jsdom has no layout, so these tests mock `clientWidth` and `clientHeight` on `HTMLElement.prototype`, as React Aria's virtualizer tests do.
  - **Bounded DOM:** with 10,000 rows, the rendered `row` count is ≤ 60.
  - **Header:** `columnheader` cells and exactly one `rowheader` per row.
  - **Keyboard:** arrow-key navigation moves focus between rows and cells.
  - **`onLoadMore` is called:**
    - once when the sentinel is visible and the state is `idle`;
    - not while `loading` or `exhausted`;
    - again after the state returns to `idle` with new rows.
  - **Error row:** retry calls `onLoadMore`.
  - **Empty rows** render `emptyState`.
  - **Row header guard:** a missing row-header column throws in development.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for `docs/features/drshya-design-system.md` (Table contract, paging responsibility, voices).

  - axe passes on `table-large` too;
  - on `table-large` the DOM row count stays ≤ 60;
  - scrolling to the bottom increments `__drshyaLoadMoreCount` exactly once.

### TASK-013 (M4): Popover, Select and ComboBox as glass overlays, with Solid fallback and full keyboard support

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **`Popover`** wraps React Aria `Popover` with the `glass` utility. Glass is allowed for popovers, per the brainstorm. Its content uses only `GLASS_TEXT_TOKENS`, and it has `rounded-control` and the glass shadow. In Solid mode it is opaque through the TASK-004 utility. Placement and flipping come from React Aria. It never opens on mount unless controlled.
  - **`Select`** uses the field anatomy plus a trigger `Button` (`nav.chevronDown`), with a `ListBox` in `Popover`. The selected option shows the `nav.check` icon. A placeholder is `ink-2` text, not `ink-3`, because it sits on glass.
  - **`ComboBox`** uses the field anatomy plus `Input`, a trigger and `ListBox` in `Popover`. It filters with the default `contains` filter from React Aria (`useFilter`). An empty result renders a "No matches" item. `allowsCustomValue` passes through.
  - Gallery entries `popover`, `select` and `combo-box`, rendered open via controlled `isOpen` / `defaultOpen` over the `surfaces-glass` busy backdrop.

  - **Popover:** Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.
  - **Glass text:** the class sets used inside popovers contain no `text-ink-3` (a static assertion over the primitives' `tv` definitions).

### TASK-014 (M4): Dialog and Menu: modal focus management that returns focus, and menus with sections and accessible destructive items

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **`Dialog`** uses React Aria `ModalOverlay` + `Modal` + `Dialog`, plus a `DialogTrigger` re-export.
    - **Surfaces:** a solid `surface` panel (rule 1: content on paper) with `rounded-frame` and a heading slot (`Heading slot="title"`, required by type).
    - **Overlay:** a `bg` color at reduced opacity through a component token (`--dialog-scrim`).
    - **Variants:** `dialog` and `alertdialog` (`role="alertdialog"` for confirmations).
    - **Dismissal:** dismissable through Escape and the outside click for `dialog` only. An `alertdialog` requires an explicit button.
    - **Focus:** it moves into the dialog on user-initiated open and returns to the trigger on close (React Aria).
  - **`Menu`** uses React Aria `MenuTrigger` + `Menu` in the glass `Popover`.
    - **Items:** `MenuItem` with an optional `icon`, `MenuSection` with a header, and `Separator`.
    - **Destructive items:** `tone="destructive"` gives `signal-failed-ink` text **and** a required icon, so meaning is not carried by color alone.
    - **Other:** disabled items and submenus through React Aria's `SubmenuTrigger` if the pinned version supports it; otherwise leave submenus out and note that here.
  - Gallery entries `dialog`, `alert-dialog` and `menu`, rendered open for screenshots.

  - **Menu:** arrow keys and typeahead work, Enter fires `onAction` and closes, disabled items are skipped, and a destructive item renders its icon and `-ink` class.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A. `packages/ui` has no session, network or storage code. The harness server in e2e binds to `127.0.0.1` only and is test infrastructure.
- **Security**:
  - **No third-party requests.** Fonts are self-hosted; the harness fails on any foreign origin (TASK-003, TASK-005).
  - **CSP compatibility.** The gallery runs under §7's `default-src 'self'`, with no inline scripts, no `data:` assets (S12) and no CSP violations.
  - **Untrusted text and URLs.** React escaping only, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` banned by lint (TASK-006), and the `Link` scheme filter (S9).
  - **Import boundary.** No Node, core or agent imports in `packages/ui` (TASK-001), so no privileged capability can reach browser code.
- **Accessibility** (plan §10 I9, §14 WCAG 2.2 AA):
  - the contrast gate for every pairing in both themes, plus the analytic glass floor (TASK-002, TASK-004);
  - `axe-core` on every gallery entry × theme × surfaces state (TASK-003);
  - the focus-visible walk (TASK-008 on);
  - state never shown by color alone (icons on every signal; tab and switch non-color cues);
  - reduced motion and reduced transparency honored;
  - focus never moved by non-user events (Toast, TASK-010).
  - **Left to later features:** manual NVDA and VoiceOver passes cover Inbox, GuardedSwitch and the timeline (FEAT-067 and FEAT-068), and 200% zoom / 320 px reflow covers app routes.
- **Error Handling**:
  - Token problems throw `TokenContractError`, a custom `Error` subclass whose message lists every failure (pairing, theme, measured versus required ratio, or an out-of-gamut token). The build and `emit:tokens --check` fail on it.
  - Primitives validate developer contracts (missing row header, icon-only button without a name) with development-time errors or warnings and typed props. Nothing is swallowed.
- **Logging**: N/A at runtime. `packages/ui` emits no logs (`no-console` with `--max-warnings=0`). The harness reports failures through test assertions and writes diff PNGs to `e2e/drshya/.out/`.
- **Parity**: N/A for FEAT-061 itself. Product words come from protocol values in later features. The icon registry and tokens are what those features render with.
